notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: the Arabic and Urdu texts are left null for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words; no published translation is quoted. Quran only: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. The chapters are a reading order built from the narrative, not a chronology the Quran claims; verses come from several surahs and surah order is not time order. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: The Quran tells its hearer to mention Idris in the scripture, and says that he was a siddiq, a word for someone of great truthfulness, and a prophet.
God raised Idris to a high place.
The Quran names Idris together with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl and says that each of them was among the patient.
God admitted them into His mercy, and the Quran says that they were among the righteous.

chapters.summary_md: The Quran tells its hearer to mention Idris, and says that he was a siddiq and a prophet [c1]. God raised him to a high place [c2]. The Quran names him with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl, each among the patient [c3].
chapters.body_md:
The Quran tells its hearer to mention Idris in the scripture, and says that he was a siddiq, a word for someone of great truthfulness, and a prophet [c1]. God raised Idris to a high place [c2].

In another passage the Quran names Idris together with Ismail and Dhul-Kifl and says that each of them was among the patient [c3]. God admitted them into His mercy, and the Quran says that they were among the righteous [c4].
chapters.deep_md: These passages say little and give no events [c1][c2][c3]. The first speaks of Idris by descriptions and an act of God: he was a siddiq and a prophet, and God raised him to a high place [c1][c2]. The later one names him in a group and gives the same descriptions to all of them: patient and righteous [c3][c4].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran tells us to remember Idris [c1]. It says he was truthful and a prophet [c1]. God raised him to a high place [c2]. The Quran also says that Idris, Ismail and Dhul-Kifl were each among the patient [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran presents Idris through his qualities, truthfulness and patience, and through what God did for him [c1][c2][c3]. Another is that being admitted into God's mercy is told of him together with others [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when or where Idris lived, who his family was, what he said or did, or how long he lived. The Quran gives no events of his life.
- Not established: what a high place means in 19:57, whether a rank or a place; the verse says only that God raised him to a high place.
- Not established: the exact sense of the Arabic word siddiq beyond great truthfulness.
- Not established: in what way each of them was patient (21:85); the verse names them and gives no events.
- Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of Idris with a figure called Enoch, and the stories told about his life. None is used in the story texts.

uncertainties_en: Hadith to add later: authenticated narrations, each with a named grader, that mention Idris. None is used in this draft.

The inventory range of Idris is 19:56-57 and 21:85-86, which are all used. The verses 21:85-86 name Ismail and Dhul-Kifl as well, and the inventory also lists 38:48 under their events; the draft uses 21:85-86 only for what they say of Idris and leaves the event link empty because the chapter also cites 19:56-57.
The sense of a high place (19:57) and of siddiq (19:56) is left open, and the draft does not say whether the raising was a rank or a place.
The Quran gives no events of his life. The draft is short on purpose and a reviewer should not expect more from these verses.
Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: the identification of Idris with Enoch. It is not used in the story texts.
Arabic and Urdu texts are not written; they are left null for translators.
